Nina (People Ops): Quick follow-up from the all-hands Q&A — drop any remaining questions about promotions, comp bands, spot bonuses, and benefit parity here. Well publish a concise FAQ + timeline by Monday. Link to slides: https://redwood.example.com/allhands/jul-2026

Pri (SWE): Two things: 1) if someone is mid-cycle on an approved relocation, which band applies? 2) are spot bonuses still discretionary vs tied to outcomes?

Sam (Comp): Relocations: we use the effective work location on file as of the payroll cut-off. If HR receives documentation before cut-off we apply local banding, otherwise it will be in the next cycle. Spot bonuses remain discretionary but we have updated guidance: must tie to measurable outcomes (incident response, ship-critical work) and include manager + peer sign-off.

Ava (Manager): For small teams — how do we ensure fair cross-team comparisons during calibration? Our work is customer-facing and hard to quantify by tokens/metrics.

Victor (Eng): Echo this — infra/ops teams often lack tidy metrics. Any suggested signals?

Nina (People Ops): Great points. For non-product teams, include 3 signals: 1) impact on uptime/incident MTTR (or qualitative description), 2) number of teams served or scale of internal adoption, 3) specific examples of ownership (oncall lead, runbook ownership, architecture decisions). A short link to a postmortem or runbook is helpful.

Pri (SWE): If a promo is approved but the person was on an extended medical leave when the decision was made, will backdating happen? We want to avoid disadvantaging folks returning from leave.

Sam (Comp): We explicitly exclude approved paid medical/parental leave from negative calibration. If promo approval overlaps with leave, comp will backdate the effective date to the standard cycle date (e.g., 8/1) and process backpay. Managers should note leave in the packet.

Ava (Manager): Is there a formal training for managers on writing equitable packets? Our engineering managers would appreciate examples.

Nina (People Ops): Yes — were running two calibration workshops next week (Wed 10am and Thu 3pm) — mandatory for new managers, recommended for all. Well record and post notes + templates.

Pri (SWE): Contractors/temps: will any comp/band changes apply to long-term contractors whove been here 18+ months? Some feel left out of benefits.

benefits-bot: Contractors: standard policy — contractors do not receive stock or full benefits. For long-term contractors, People Ops evaluates extended engagement allowances and spot bonuses on a case-by-case basis.

Sam (Comp): Adding: if a contractor is converting to FTE and a market move is in progress, comp will try to align the conversion offer to the adjusted band, but final offers are subject to hiring budget and approvals.

Pri (SWE): Appeal window? Is it still 10 business days and manager-submitted?

Nina (People Ops): Yes, 10 business days post-letters; manager-submitted appeals only. Provide new, verifiable evidence (metrics, customer emails, review links). Well log all appeals and share anonymized outcomes in the post-cycle report.

Ava (Manager): Any change to how we communicate denials to employees? We want to keep coaching-focused language.

Nina (People Ops): Managers should provide a development-oriented note with clear next steps and suggested timelines (e.g., milestones for re-nom). People Ops will share a short script + examples to standardize language.

benefits-bot: Payroll cut-off reminder: August payroll cut-off = 2026-07-18. Changes confirmed after that will post in September.

Nina (People Ops): Action items: managers -> flag relocations/leave in packets, attach links for non-metric teams, join calibration workshop if possible, and use the short packet template. Well post the FAQ, manager script examples, and workshop recordings by Monday EOD. Thanks everyone! :bow:
